title: Architecture Constraint
description: The frontmatter of constraints/<constraint-slug>.md (SPEC-003). No subtypes. A constraint limits the solution space, never the domain: integration strategies, technology bounds, quality demands. What it cannot be is a domain rule wearing an architecture name — that is a Rule. Nor is it a project's own arrangement convention wearing a system-wide name: a constraint holds what the solution must have regardless of which project or stack encodes it, and how one project's source achieves that — even the identical property — is a standard's rule, never a second entry here. The body carries `## Description`.

statement.description: One falsifiable condition over the implementation.

scope.description: `system`, or the context slug the constraint is confined to.

fitness.description: The mechanical check that verifies the constraint, where one exists.

examples.statement: Events between contexts travel asynchronously; no context calls another synchronously to publish a fact.
